input: nums is a list of n nonnegative integers, 0 <= n <= 4294967295. Each value gives the maximum forward jump distance from its zero-based index; every index + nums[index] must be <= 9007199254740991. Zero distances and empty input are accepted. String inputs, when present, are ordinary str values, not subclasses. Integer values are plain int, excluding bool; lists are ordinary lists, not subclasses. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Allocation and runtime resource limits still require qualification; this declared domain is not a capacity or completion guarantee.
return: Boolean indicating whether the final index can be reached from index 0 using jumps of any integer length from 0 through the value at the departure index. A singleton returns true even with value zero; empty input returns false because it has no start or final index.
mutation_aliasing: All inputs, their ordering and caller-owned containers remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state, and separate calls share no mutable result state. Only scalar reachability state is retained during the call.
numeric: All distances, indices, index + distance and farthest remain nonnegative safe integers by precondition. Python arbitrary-size integers do not broaden this paired domain. The last-index sentinel is -1 for empty input.
complexity: O(n + 1) worst-case time and O(1) auxiliary space. Before each index is used, it must be no larger than the farthest reachable index. Reach is monotonically extended, and the method returns as soon as the last index is reachable or a gap is found.
